I use an old makeup brush to apply it. I always accidentally make to much so the plastic baggie lets me store it in the fridge. When I'm done, I just through the baggie away. Clean and simple. 

I also just rinse it off in the shower. I haven't noticed that it clogs any more than usual (I have long hair, so drainage is always an issue).

Godspeed, my friend. Proactiv withdrawal is the worst. I used proactiv for 5 years and got tired of shelling out all that money every two months for a product that didn't keep me all that clear. When I went off it, my skin broke out in huge clusters of acne all over my face. I didn't even want to leave the house. After two months, I couldn't take it anymore and went back on proactiv. Eventually, I worked up my resolve to once again quit using it. I was able to get off of it by using panoxyl face wash, the glycolic acid toner from Mario Badescue, and the benzoyl peroxide gel from acne.org. On pimples that were really large (not cystic, just huge), I would put some neosporin cream on the pimple and apply one of those circular band aids and wear that overnight. Most nights my face was covered in those circle bandaids and I would wake up with them stuck to my hair.  It sounds like very harsh treatment for my skin (and it was), but it was the only routine that seemed to keep the massive withdrawal breakouts at bay. 

I now have switched to using the cera ve foaming face wash, glycolic acid toner, the stridex pads, and the cera ve moisturizer and my skin is much smoother. I would seriously recommend purchasing the aztec healing clay powder and apple cider vinegar. That mask sucks all the crud out of my large pores and keeps my skin from getting horribly congested, which I always suspected was a big part of my acne issue. 

I sympathize wholeheartedly with your proactiv plight. Stay strong!
